conviction_note: abs_move 16 (option event-implied 15.76%, own median 13.16%, last three prints +11/+35/+48) times a slight up lean, p_up 53: a crowded short (10.0M shares, 8.9 days to cover), call-heavy options, and three straight quarters of beating its own EBITDA guide outweigh a collapsing PC market and peers selling off on holiday guides. impact_sum +1.8 is the sum of nine small, mostly proxy findings and is larger than the scaled +0.96 because the guidance-line risk (Q4 implied by the FY range, PC units forecast -24 to -27% for Q4) is the line that decided last year's Q3 print (-13.2%) and it carries the uncertainty that p_up holds near 50.
bar: Q3 2026 company guide: net revenue $320-350M, adjusted EBITDA $18-21M, non-GAAP EPS $0.09-0.12 (8-K ex99.1, 2026-08-06, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001743759/000119312526337943/crsr-ex99_1.htm). Consensus revenue $332-343M and EPS $0.10-0.12 across aggregators (Chartmill $343.3M/$0.12 https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CRSR/estimates ; MarketBeat $332.2M/$0.10 https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/corsair-gaming-nasdaqcrsr-updates-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-2026-08-06/ ; Benzinga $337.1M/$0.11 https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CRSR/earnings-forecasts). The sources roughly agree and the bar sits at or above the guide midpoint. FY2026 guide $1.40-1.47B revenue, adj EBITDA $121-131M, non-GAAP EPS $0.85-0.94. With Q1 ($354.5M / $35.8M) and Q2 ($314.3M / $30.8M), that implies a Q4 of about $431M revenue and about $40M adj EBITDA at the midpoints, against Q4 2025's $436.9M / $53.6M. That implied Q4 is the guidance bar.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 10,040,571 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 8.86 days to cover (9.66M / 9.84 DTC at 09-30), about 9.3% of shares outstanding. Free float is much smaller than shares outstanding (majority holder EagleTree), so short interest as a share of float is materially higher; I found no sourced float figure. Source: https://equibles.com/stocks/crsr/shortinterest (read 2026-11-05). Options: 25-delta skew -11.91 vol points (calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI ratio 0.21, ATM IV 115%, event-implied move 15.76% (sealed baseline). Positioning: a crowded short sits under a call-heavy, bullish option market, both into a print. The stock is 11.7% below its 52-week high and fell 7.7% over 5 days.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 PC unit shipments fell 20.1% YoY (IDC, Oct 8) to 22.4% (Gartner, Oct 12) on memory-cost-driven price rises, and Omdia/Counterpoint forecast another 24-27% decline in Q4. Corsair's FY guide still implies a Q4 of about $431M revenue and about $40M adj EBITDA, down only about 1% YoY on revenue. Its Gaming Components & Systems segment (63% of Q2 revenue) is guided to decline low double digits. The risk lands on the FY/Q4 guide, the line that sank last year's Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-04): revenue miss plus a lowered full-year guide, stock -13.16% (baseline; https://www.itiger.com/news/1192909105). Q2 2026 raised the FY guide and the stock rose +35.25%; Q4 2025 guided FY26 EBITDA growth and it rose +48.25%. This name moves hard on the FY range.
findings.why_not_priced: Corsair has not spoken since Aug 6, before these Q3 unit data and the Q4 forecasts were published, so the FY range has not been tested against them. If the market had priced a Q4 cut, puts would be bid. Instead skew is -11.9 (calls bid) and put/call OI is 0.21. The 5-day -7.7% drift is the only sign of it.
findings.independence: This is a proxy: OEM PC units are not Corsair's DIY channel, and IDC attributes part of the drop to early-2026 stockpiling, which may not apply to DIY. Same direction: IDC preliminary 20.1% (https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/22264/pc-shipments-fall-20-1-idc) and Logitech's CEO citing a 20% fall in PC shipments (https://www.tikr.com/blog/logitech-sinks-11-on-weak-holiday-guidance-as-chip-supplier-incident-bites-fortunately-q3-carries-the-brunt). Offsetting (lesson 9): the peripherals segment (37%) is guided up low double digits, and memory revenue rises with ASP (+17% YoY in Q2). The size is net of those.

findings.finding: Logitech's Q2 FY27 (quarter to Sep 30, released Oct 27) grew sales 3% to $1.22B, its 11th straight growth quarter, with Gaming a named growth driver and mice/keyboards up mid-single digits while PC shipments fell 20%. Peripheral end-demand held through September, which bears on Corsair's peripherals segment (guided +low double digits for Q3).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Corsair peripherals beat in Q1 (+10%) and Q2 (+13%) of 2026, and the stock rose +11.1% and +35.3% on those prints. Peripherals fell in Q4 2025 and the stock still rose +48% on margin and guide.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's quarter reported after Corsair last spoke, so Q3 consensus ($332-343M) was set before it. But Logitech fell 11-12% on its holiday guide, so read-through sentiment was negative, not positive. CRSR's 5-day -7.7% is consistent with sympathy selling, not with having priced healthy Q3 peripheral demand.
findings.independence: Shares a document set with the supplier-incident finding (Logitech's Oct 27 release), but these are different facts: demand here, supply there. Supporting: https://www.tikr.com/blog/logitech-sinks-11-on-weak-holiday-guidance-as-chip-supplier-incident-bites-fortunately-q3-carries-the-brunt (mice and keyboards grew mid-single digits).

findings.finding: Logitech disclosed that an unnamed semiconductor supplier's plant closed at the end of June after a serious incident, reopened in September, and is still below required capacity. Logitech's Dec-quarter guide carries a $70-80M sales hit (it warned of up to $200M in July), and its stock fell 11-12%. Corsair did not mention any supplier problem on its Aug 6 call, and its exposure to the same supplier is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Corsair supply-disruption print in the baseline window; the 2025-11-04 guide cut (-13.2%) is the nearest analogue on the guidance line.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed Corsair shared the supplier, CRSR would have gapped with LOGI on Oct 28 and puts would be bid. The skew instead pays for upside.
findings.independence: Same Logitech release as the demand finding. Second source on the incident: https://247wallst.com/cards/logitech-q2-2027-earnings-logi-01m5zg0kygyhbj99fgs2mqk5vc. Nothing ties it to Corsair, so this is an inference with no confirmation.

findings.finding: Retail DDR5 kit prices kept rising through Q3: a mainstream 32GB DDR5 kit starts about $350-450 in October 2026, against about $100-200 a year earlier (Tom's Hardware RAM price index; Newegg $399-479). Corsair's memory revenue was +17% YoY in Q2 on ASP and North American share gains, with supply 'adequate'. A memory module maker's Q3 revenue rises with kit ASP, pointing to components revenue at or above the 'declines low double digits' guide. TrendForce's Q4 contract increase slows to about +20% QoQ from about 80%/40%, and management already guided memory gross margin down to the high teens in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 memory +24% drove a components beat and the stock rose +48.25%. Q2 2026 memory +17% and the stock rose +35.25% (with the guide raise).
findings.source_date: 2026-10-14 (price observation as quoted in search snippet; snippet_only, page not fetched)
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 guide was set Aug 6, assuming a components decline. Retail kit prices rose further after that, so consensus revenue ($332-343M) brackets the guide midpoint rather than above it. If priced, consensus would sit near the top of the $320-350M range.
findings.independence: A proxy (retail price series, not Corsair's own number). Newegg insider, Oct 2026: https://www.newegg.com/insider/?p=93717. Against it: unit demand destruction (DDR5 kits sitting on shelves, https://www.tweaktown.com/news/110989/ddr5-memory-and-ssds-sit-on-retail-shelves-as-128gb-kit-prices-hit-4-200/index.html) and an early European retail decline report, which risks an inventory margin squeeze. Sized net of both.

findings.finding: Short interest is 10.04M shares with 8.86 days to cover (2026-10-15 settlement), rising from 9.25M at 09-15, on a name whose float is well below its share count. The option market is call-heavy (put/call OI 0.21, skew -11.9 vol points). The last three prints moved +48%, +11% and +35%. An in-line-or-better print with the FY range held has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 5 of 7 prints up, median |move| 13.16%. Up-moves after beats were +48.25 (Feb 2026), +11.14 (May 2026) and +35.25 (Aug 2026). Down-moves were -13.16 (Nov 2025 guide cut) and -0.29.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest rose into the print, so shorts have not covered. Calls are bid, so longs are leaning the same way; the finding is the asymmetry of a short at 8.9 days to cover against a print-day move distribution skewed up. If priced, DTC would have fallen and skew normalised.
findings.independence: Option data from the sealed baseline (Yahoo chain, a different source from FINRA via equibles). The two point the same way.

findings.finding: Q2's adjusted EBITDA ($30.8M) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.23) included a one-off $15.6M IEEPA tariff refund ($14.3M EBITDA, $0.14 EPS) that the company calls 'materially complete'. Q3 has no such item, so headline YoY and QoQ comparisons will look weaker (Q3 EPS guide $0.09-0.12 against Q2's $0.23). The guide already excludes the refund.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Aug 2026 the refund was disclosed alongside a raised guide and the stock rose +35%. Holders bought the guide, not the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: it sits inside the company's guide and consensus ($0.10-0.12). The only residual is headline-optics on algorithmic first reads.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript confirms the figures: https://www.webull.com/news/15398317698327552.

findings.finding: GTA VI's November 19, 2026 launch, which management named as a Q4 console-peripheral tailwind in the raised FY guide, has been repeatedly reaffirmed by Take-Two, and I found no further delay. One support for the implied Q4 is intact going into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 guide raise that cited GTA 6 was bought (+35.25%).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it was already in the Aug 6 guide. Its value is only that no delay has removed it since.
findings.independence: Q2 call names GTA 6 as a Q4 tailwind: https://www.webull.com/news/15398317698327552. Take-Two reiterations: https://www.tomsguide.com/gaming/gta-6-is-on-track-for-its-november-release-date-but-we-might-be-waiting-a-while-for-the-next-trailer

findings.finding: October sell-side and quant activity was mixed and small: Argus set a $15 price target on 2026-10-14 (spot $12.67), and Wall Street Zen's quant rating was cut on 2026-10-24. No broker preview or estimate cut surfaced.
findings.why_not_priced: Public rating changes are priced. Filed for completeness so judges can see the bar was not cut into the print.

findings.finding: In 2026 Corsair has beaten the top of its own adjusted EBITDA guide every quarter: Q4 2025 $53.6M ('above the high end'), Q1 2026 $35.8M against a $25-30M guide, and Q2 2026 $16.6M ex-refund against $12.5-15.5M. That is a conservative guide-setting habit applied to the Q3 range of $18-21M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The three prints that beat the EBITDA top end moved +48.25%, +11.14% and +35.25%. The last miss-and-cut, Q3 2025, moved -13.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.10-0.12 sits inside the $0.09-0.12 guide rather than above it, so the street has not extrapolated the beat habit. If it had, consensus would sit above the top end.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1743759/000119312526048668/crsr-ex99_1.htm ; Q2 2026 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001743759/000119312526337943/crsr-ex99_1.htm. These are the company's own documents, each a separate filing.

rejected_candidates.detail: Pre-dates the Aug 6 guide, and management already cited 'delayed DIY demand'. Merged into the PC/DIY guidance finding.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees: the up-paid skew, call-heavy OI and rising short interest point the same way as the beat-habit and memory findings. The one finding that cuts against them, PC units collapsing into a Q4 the FY guide still implies, is the line that produced last year's -13% Q3 reaction. That keeps p_up near 50 despite the skew.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest) and lesson 7 (negative against a call-bid skew on a short with 8.9 days to cover): PC-units guidance finding shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0
Lesson 5 (proxy is smaller): DRAM retail price finding shrunk from +1.0 to +0.8, because it is a retail series, not Corsair's number
Lesson 2 (one-off inside guidance): tariff-refund comparison cut from -0.2 to -0.1
Lessons 1 and 8 left the beat-habit (+0.7) and positioning (+1.0) findings standing: this name has paid for beats on the line (+48/+11/+35), and abs_move kept at 16, not shrunk
p_up and abs_move unchanged (53, 16), so expected_move_pct is unchanged at +0.96
